name: Top-Down Memoized DFS
summary: Ask recursively 'can the rest of the string from position i be built from dictionary words?', trying each word as a prefix, and cache each position's yes/no answer so it is solved once.
visualizationIntent: init: show s as characters; every position starts unknown, with the empty suffix (past the end) marked breakable. recurse: the i cursor marks the position being solved; the end cursor marks the prefix being tested; the call-stack panel shows depth. check: if a prefix equals a dictionary word, recurse on the remainder. update: a position turns green when breakable, red when a dead end, and is reused if revisited. return: whether position 0 is breakable.

lineExplanations.4: A memo of each position: 0 unknown, 1 breakable, -1 dead end.
lineExplanations.5: The empty suffix past the end is trivially breakable.
lineExplanations.6: Ask whether the whole string (from position 0) can be segmented.
lineExplanations.10: If this position was already solved, reuse the cached result.
lineExplanations.12: Assume this position is a dead end until a word fits.
lineExplanations.13: Try each dictionary word as the next piece.
lineExplanations.14: Where the word would end if placed here.
lineExplanations.15: The word must fit within the string.
lineExplanations.16: The prefix starting here must equal the word.
lineExplanations.17: Recurse: can the remainder after this word be segmented?
lineExplanations.18: If so, this position is breakable.
lineExplanations.19: Record whether any word led to a full segmentation.
lineExplanations.22: Mark this position a dead end.
lineExplanations.23: Return whether this position can be segmented.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def wordBreak(self, s, wordDict): receives the string and the dictionary.
syntaxExplanations.3: n = len(s) stores the string length.
syntaxExplanations.4: memo = [0] * (n + 1) makes an unknown slot per position.
syntaxExplanations.5: memo[n] = 1 marks the empty suffix breakable.
syntaxExplanations.6: answer = self.solve(s, wordDict, 0, memo, n) starts the recursion at position 0.
syntaxExplanations.7: return answer reports the final yes/no.
syntaxExplanations.9: def solve(self, s, wordDict, i, memo, n): decides if s from position i is breakable.
syntaxExplanations.10: if memo[i] != 0: is true when this position was already solved.
syntaxExplanations.11: return memo[i] == 1 reuses the cached yes/no.
syntaxExplanations.12: found = False assumes a dead end until a word works.
syntaxExplanations.13: for word in wordDict: tries each dictionary word.
syntaxExplanations.14: end = i + len(word) is where the word would end.
syntaxExplanations.15: if end <= n: keeps the word inside the string.
syntaxExplanations.16: if s[i:end] == word: checks the prefix matches the word.
syntaxExplanations.17: if self.solve(s, wordDict, end, memo, n): recurses on the remainder.
syntaxExplanations.18: found = True records a successful segmentation.
syntaxExplanations.19: if found: is true when some word led to a full break.
syntaxExplanations.20: memo[i] = 1 caches this position as breakable.
syntaxExplanations.22: memo[i] = -1 caches this position as a dead end.
syntaxExplanations.23: return found hands the answer back to the caller.
